answer: Sybil resistance comes from charging for the beacon itself: every epoch a claim carries a beacon transaction priced in POA locked until peers attest two randomly drawn epochs of prior work. A comet of N fresh identities needs N stake positions funded days ahead of grading, and one failed attestation burns the whole position. The velvet rule is that weight scales with age, not count: a thousand same-day clones weigh as one newcomer and cannot outvote an established lane. Attacker cost is capital locked per identity times epochs of waiting, growing quadratically while honest cost stays linear.
